newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal-Basis offers steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal-Basis offers steady to higher.

text.p: Basis offers in U.S. cash soymeal markets were steady to higher on Friday in response to robust end-user demand, dealers said.
"Some of these guys that have been out of the market for a while now are finally having to step back in and buy meal," said one dealer in Indiana.
Merchandisers said meal inventories were generally in good shape and there were few back-ups in supply despite a higher-than-expected weekly crush.
"I think everybody is in good shape," said an Illinois crusher. "We've finally cleared up our rail meal."
The National Oilseed Processors Association put the crush for the week ended Wednesday at larger-than-expected 23.891 million bushels.
That figure fell at the high end of expectations for 20.25 to 24.00 million bushels and was sharply above last week's pace of 21.871 million.
The increase in the crush was caused by a recent jump in crushing margins, brokers said.
